newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian palm olein rises in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian palm olein rises in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian palm oleim prices rose in late trading on Friday due to the weaker rupiah but most players stayed out of the market due to uncertainty in the local currency, traders said.
They said palm olein was quoted at 1,570 rupiah/kg in Jakarta against 1,540 in the morning. Crude palm oil stayed at 1,285 rupiah/kg in North Sumatran city of Medan.
"Most traders stayed out the market because of the uncertainty in the currency. Players do want to buy while sellers are holding back," said one trader.
"We are waiting to see what's going to happen with the rupiah next week before taking further decisions. We just do not want to take any risks," said one trader.
Some traders attempted to sell oil in dollars, but buyers ignored them, said the traders.
The rupiah fell to a historic low of 2,915 against the dollar in afternoon trading following the central bank's move on Thursday to scrap its intervention band. It had since recovered slightly.

Traders said they largely ignored developments in Malaysia, where prices surged on strong buying by players attracted by the weak value of the ringgit and supportive crop and export data from the government.
